author: Mark Atwood
text:
2026-11-27: this bead's secure_delete guarantee is now EVENTUAL, not immediate (decision mimid-1wgh.134).

The agent's database runs in a write-ahead log. secure_delete still zeroes a freed page, but the zeroed page goes to mimid.sqlite-wal while mimid.sqlite keeps the page that carried the old text until a checkpoint copies the frame back. So a destroyed chat's text is gone from the database's files once the log is checkpointed and reset, and until then it is readable on disk -- in mimid.sqlite itself, not only in the log, which is the part the decision bead first had wrong. Nothing checkpoints on the delete path: Mark took the fsyncs (48 write transactions and 192 fsyncs for one first private message before, 49 after; the client's echo 35.8 s to 11.2 s under I/O pressure) over wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) per destroy, with the weaker guarantee stated.

agent-frontends.md 7.9 now says this, and 7.37 records the decision. tests/chat_delete.rs still asserts the property in its eventual form: it checkpoints and truncates the log, then requires the text in none of mimid.sqlite, -wal or -shm. Removing the checkpoint from that test makes it fail with "mimid.sqlite holds \"gone text\"", so the bytes are demonstrably there before the checkpoint and gone after.

What is no longer covered: the window between the delete's commit and the next checkpoint. A daemon stopped cleanly checkpoints and leaves nothing; a daemon running, or killed, keeps the text.
